allocation.question: On a credential-free substrate, can an independently justified end-to-end product-economics counter (measured per-operation cost such as model calls/tokens, browser/network work, retrieval, verification and repair, rather than the preregistered abstract equal-weight {http_requests, retrieval_calls, verification_calls, repair_attempts} counter) be constructed and measured so that reuse-based localized repair is or is not strictly cheaper than cold re-derivation at L=2 and L=3 — i.e. is the observed counter-dependence a genuine product-economics boundary, or an artifact of an equal-weight counter no external agent actually uses — and therefore should localized repair be permanently dropped from the C-PRODUCT-ECON product story?
allocation.rationale: Reactivates IDLE Runtime on the shared validity blocker both Runtime and Graph handoffs converged on. Decision counterfactual: an independently justified counter showing strict reuse win at L=2/L=3 re-admits localized repair to the product story with a stated counter; failure to construct one, or a measured loss under every justifiable weighting (predeclared weight grid), permanently drops local repair from C-PRODUCT-ECON and stops cross-lane rediscovery of the same counter artifact. Strongest baseline is cold re-derivation at matched success with contamination bounds. Smallest batch: same fetch-scarce substrate and shipped carrier held fixed, counter-weighting robustness only. Stop trigger: another equal-weight-only rerun without the independent counter → park thread.
